items.title: Skitch Henderson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Milford, Connecticut, October 31, 1998
items.q: I brought men like... Clark Terry from the Ellington band... Well it started about the time that I brought Clark in... Clark Terry was — Clark and Snooky were the greatest disciples that ever came along.

ctx.x: —how the philosophy changes. Now it’s the elite job in New York. But at that time, they really didn’t want a staff job either. It was strange. They didn’t know where to go or what to do. So I brought men like, well I could start with Doc Carl Severinsen. I took him from Charlie Barnet’s band, and Clark Terry from the Ellington band, Tommy Newsom was with the Navy band in Washington, Hymie Schertzer had been with the Goodman band, I mean I could go through the whole, Bobby Haggart of course of fame, the best bass…
I’ll tell him that. You actually referred to him as the Chairman of the Board of the Time Factory.

items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Skitch Henderson was the conductor of “The Tonight Show,” music director. I said, “Aaron, I tell you. I happen to know”, because we live close to each other. We came to work every day.

ctx.x: But as far as being a staff musician.

That’s right, yeah. You have to understand now. Each network has 175 musicians. So this went on beautifully for a while, and the Urban League pressured them a little more. Said, “I think you can do a little better than that.” So now, Aaron

Levine comes to me. “Clark, you got any of your buddies there that can play first trumpet, great solos, and has a family, has children,” and he has to be a certain age, has to be – there’s about 15 prerequisites that he laid down. He just couldn’t be another cat. I had to rack my brain to think of somebody that could fill those shoes. Finally I came up with Snooky Young, who had just came out of retirement and gone back with Basie’s band. I called Snooky’s family, and they said, “Oh yeah, Uncle Clark. We got to…
